propositions: Strict CAS push delivery raises catchable PushDeliveryError with stable reason codes and unpushed-commit detail, translating to nonzero exit only at the Python module adapter boundary.

Core retry budget enforces exactly five push-first cycles; only retriable non-fast-forward rejection triggers fetch-merge recovery; successful recovery earns exactly one conditional sixth push, earlier success exits without it.

Opt-in strict delivery is additive with keyword-only API and strict=False default; all pre-existing callers across library, CLI, MCP, importer, and store-write paths retain best-effort disposition and legacy return contracts.
Strict failure preserves working tree state, omits ticket events and BRIDGE_ALERT, and leaves unpushed commits reachable; paired best-effort calls return None under identical fault conditions.
Default best-effort behavior remains unchanged across event append, batch append, NDJSON import, transition close, both delete paths, both compact paths, and claim operations.
Policy declines and transport failures are classified as distinct stable reasons with separate git/config detail for operational visibility without changing error vocabulary.
